meaning: Interpretive argument that the strong per se reading is what St. Thomas meant. A transcription (invariant 16): the textual premises and the charity principle are opaque propositions, and the proof applies the charity principle to them, so Lean verifies only that the conclusion was transcribed. Both formal premises are premise-free results of their own: AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-STRONG-READING-YIELDS-UNMOVED-MOVER, and AQUINAS-ST-I-Q2-A3-WEAK-READING-DOES-NOT-YIELD-UNMOVED-MOVER (a finite model in which every mover is moved in some respect). The textual premises and the charity principle remain source-fidelity and methodology claims; on reading B of q.46 a.2 ad 7 the no-counter-evidence premise fails.
